attempts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: ONE cohesive FOUR-VIEW TURNAROUND BOARD for the Stardew Valley BARN, for reviewing the architecture before making game sprites.
Reference image 1 is the actual Barn sprite atlas. Copy its visual identity: modest weathered warm-brown rounded/gambrel shingle roof, red vertical-board walls, ochre framing, narrow wooden human door, broad animal opening, small attached timber lean-to on its original right side. Use only the upper 112x112 building; ignore loose animation parts in the bottom strip.
Reference image 2 is the STRUCTURAL AUTHORITY for all four views. It shows a single estimated solid building rotated under a fixed game camera. Preserve its four silhouettes, horizontal/vertical ground directions, relative proportions, roof-ridge orientation, same scale and placement of the attached structure. Render these four volumes in the reference sprite's pixel-art style. Do not redesign them into four unrelated houses.
Board layout: 2x2, FRONT top left, LEFT top right, RIGHT bottom left, BACK bottom right. A short title BARN and those four simple labels only. Generous even spacing on a plain light warm-gray background. Crisp high-resolution board, ideally 2048x1536.
FRONT: reproduce the recognizable original front, with small human door left and wide animal entry center-right; lean-to at right.
LEFT (original front faces screen-left): the roof RIDGE now runs HORIZONTALLY across the narrow sprite, exactly as the guide. We see the broad roof SLOPE and a side wall/near lean-to, not the original arched front gable. The attached lean-to is near the camera and is visible toward the bottom, as in the guide.
RIGHT (original front faces screen-right): horizontal roof ridge and roof slope again; the near side wall is closed red planks. The attached lean-to has rotated to the FAR end and is mostly hidden. This view is structurally different from LEFT; do not simply mirror it.
BACK: original front faces away/up; opaque closed red back wall without invented entrances, attached structure at left, roof consistent with FRONT.
Do not force the front doors to remain visible in strict side/back views. They remain on the original entrance wall, edge-on or hidden; never paste a front doorway onto the side wall. Door visibility for gameplay will be redesigned separately.
Use the authentic compact low-resolution pixel-art vocabulary of image 1: limited palette, blocky clean shading, square stepped outlines, small readable shingle clusters. Avoid painterly texture noise, smoothing, glossy 3D, photographic lighting and a new fancy fantasy design.
All four states are fully OPAQUE. No Reveal, no cutaway, no transparency demonstration, no checkerboard. No terrain, people, animals, furniture, detached props, collision grids, arrows or dimension text. This is an artistic turnaround board, not a map planner or an engineering diagram. The guide controls the geometry; the original sprite controls materials and style.

Use case: stylized-concept.

Image 1 is the original Shed sprite, the visual identity reference: warm golden horizontal-log walls, thick ochre corner timbers, a compact central red wooden door, small dark attic vent directly above it, and the tall rounded/pointed red-orange overlapping shingle roof. Preserve this particular Shed, not the red-walled Barn.
Image 2 is the STRUCTURAL AUTHORITY. It rotates the same volume under a fixed elevated tile-game camera. Follow its four silhouettes, roof ridges, roof-plane directions, relative widths/depths and equal scale. The source footprint is 7 wide by 3 deep, so the left/right states are much narrower than front/back.
Make a clean 2x2 board: FRONT top left, LEFT top right, RIGHT bottom left, BACK bottom right. Title SHED, only those four labels, plain light warm-gray background, ideally 2048x1536. Keep equal world scale and camera elevation, not equal sprite widths.
FRONT: original red door and small vent centered on the wooden gable façade.
LEFT and RIGHT: TRUE side-facing redraws. The roof ridge runs HORIZONTALLY across the narrow building, the roof slope occupies the upper body as in the structure guide, and the low visible eave-side wall at the bottom is horizontal-log timber. No peaked front gable pointing at the viewer in these side panels. No central front door or attic vent pasted onto a side wall. The original entrance is edge-on to the left or right and can be hidden.
BACK: closed timber gable wall without human door or copied front vent; same roof, timberwork, heights and materials as the front. Do not invent rear doors or architectural extensions.
Image 2 has flat construction colors only: replace these with the pixel-art surface treatment of image 1. Overlapping RED SHINGLES must read as a sloped roof, with gently changing band shading and depth toward the eave, not a brick wall. Use clean stepped pixel outlines, limited warm palette, compact source-like details and consistent soft daylight.
Opaque ordinary appearance throughout. No transparency, Reveal, cutaway, terrain, checkerboard, people, animals, ground platforms, flower boxes, extra windows, side doors, extra buildings, arrows or dimensional labels. Do not angle the entire building into isometric three-quarter views to show the door.

Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: ONE FOUR-VIEW TURNAROUND BOARD of the actual Stardew Valley STABLE.
Reference image 1 is the source Stable sprite, defining its identity: a small OPEN timber stall with a SINGLE-SLOPE red/rust panel roof, tall rough golden-brown wooden posts, back planks, side rails/braces, a little hay and the modest original blue bucket detail. There is no horse in this asset, no human entrance door, no enclosed shed façade and no peaked gable roof.
Reference image 2 is the STRUCTURAL AUTHORITY. It shows the SAME estimated structure rotated under one fixed elevated tile-game camera. Keep its single roof plane, the reversal of the roof's visible slope between front and back, same scale, four ground orientations and closed-back/open-front distinction.
Compose a 2x2 review board with FRONT top left, LEFT top right, RIGHT bottom left, BACK bottom right. Title STABLE, only those four labels. Plain warm pale-gray background with even spacing, ideally 2048x1536.
FRONT: original open stall between two substantial wooden posts, sloping roof higher at screen-right, back timbers visible inside. Keep the center entrance open and unobstructed. Use only the original small hay/bucket details where they make sense.
LEFT and RIGHT: narrow side views corresponding to a 2-wide by 4-deep footprint. Roof and posts rotate together; the broad open front is edge-on and must not be pasted onto the side. Show the appropriate side rail/cross brace and the single sloped roof plane. Match the high/low end relationship to the guide. Keep LEFT and RIGHT consistent with the same physical shelter.
BACK: roof high/low edge reverses horizontally relative to FRONT, enclosed wooden back wall, no copied front stall opening, no invented door.
The front/back are 4 tiles wide, the sides 2; don't widen the sides to make another front view. Do not add lean-tos, gabled roofs, extra stalls, closed red doors, extra windows, barn walls, a paddock or extra animals. The structural guide is simple on purpose; the source sprite supplies the materials and recognizable details.
Compact hand-placed pixel-art clusters and stepped outlines, source-like warm palette and readable dark timber outlines. Consistent low-resolution game aesthetic, no painterly noise, glossy 3D, smoothing or realistic architectural perspective. Fully opaque all four views. No cutaway, Reveal, checkerboard, alpha demonstration, ground tiles, arrows or measurement labels.
